Per the project's recorded convention, a release is a git tag.

1. Make sure `main` has what you want to ship. Run `make test-fast` first if you want a sanity check.
2. Tag the commit as `vYYYY.MM.N`. `N` is the release counter within that month. For example, `v2026.09.2` was the second release in September 2026. Since today is 2026-10-01, the first October release would be `v2026.10.1`.
3. Push the tag, for example `git tag v2026.10.1 && git push origin v2026.10.1`.
4. CI builds and publishes from the tag. Never publish by hand.

I found this in the project's memory store, where it's recorded as a human-authored convention. I didn't find a CI workflow or release script in the repo to confirm it. I also don't know how to pick `N` beyond counting the month's existing tags. Run `git tag --list 'v2026.10.*'` to see which numbers are taken. I haven't created or pushed any tag.
